=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:408-416 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When the re-listing in `_reopen_tracker_after_post` fails, the function now raises `ApiError` even though the entry comment was already posted (:480-483), so `upsert` exits 2 and scripts/activation_verify.sh:753-759 sends an inaccurate "could not be updated" WARNING and does `return 0` before the verdict comment at :762-769 is built or posted.
  WHY: One transient GitHub failure after a successful entry post drops the `<!-- ai:activation:v1 verdict=... -->` marker with no automatic retry (PR mode needs a re-run, and project mode gets no trusted marker), and the same raise makes unblock_judge record `ops_failed` for a write that landed; severity disagreement: minimax=MAJOR, sonnet/gemini/glm=NIT, so the highest is used.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:638-648 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_is_release_entry` classifies an unticked step with no `dormant_until` as release-only from its title alone (`not dormant and RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE.match(title)`, regex at :592-596), and `dormant_until` is optional, so a real human step such as "Sync the DEPLOY_TOKEN secret to the stable environment" can match.
  WHY: Once `stable` contains the commit, `resolve` ticks the human step and, if no other unticked box is left, closes the tracker (:782), so the manual work is skipped and nobody is notified (glm declined to re-flag this, calling it documented intended behaviour that the last-run diff did not modify).
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:762-801 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The never-close-again guard at :762 keys on `state_reason == "reopened"`, but the pipeline's own reopen PATCHes (:415, :797, :801; `-f state=open` only) neither set nor distinguish that field, and the new fail-safe at :792-799 reopens the tracker on any transient post-close comment-read failure.
  WHY: If GitHub reports `reopened`, one transient read error strands the tracker: it logs `outcome=open reason=reopened` forever and never auto-closes, against the plan's "The issue closes when no unticked boxes remain"; if it reports `null`/`completed`, the pipeline's own reopen is undone on the next tick; the test fake hard-codes `state_reason="reopened"` (tests/test_operator_step_issue.py:71-76), so the tests cannot detect either case (glm says this trade-off was accepted as won't-fix in the previous round, CONSOLIDATOR_OVERRIDDEN: iss_731ab74d16e9efd0).
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:700-793 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `resolve()` reads the tracker state only once (:700) and checks the `reopened` guard against that snapshot (:762) before the close PATCH (:782); the post-close re-read (:793) checks comments only, never the issue state.
  WHY: A person who closes and reopens the tracker during the identity, comment and up-to-10 compare round trips has the reopen overwritten with `state_reason=completed`, which breaks "a tracker someone reopened is never closed"; severity disagreement: gemini/luna=MAJOR, minimax=NIT (glm calls the residual window at :785-791 documented and accepted).
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:345 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Prepending `Note: ` to lines that match DORMANT_LINE_RE means `_unticked_steps` no longer recognises those lines as dormant lines.
  WHY: Tracker resolution misreads release steps as human steps because it cannot find their dormant condition, so the tracker either closes too early or fails to resolve.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:338-346 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new `Note: ` prefix in `render_entry` changes the rendered body of existing entries whose instructions contain a dormant-shaped line, so the `upsert` body-equality check (:478-482) posts a superseding comment.
  WHY: Affected keys get a one-time duplicate authoritative entry comment (extra writes, and harmless for `resolve`), and the changelog, README and agents fragment do not mention it.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:752-754 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: When the after-close read fails, the code logs an error and raises an ApiError, so the process exits 2.
  WHY: Callers wrongly report the write as failed, which misleads operators.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:792-799 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fail-safe reopen PATCH at :797 inside the new `except ApiError` handler is unguarded, so if it fails its error replaces the original and the tracker stays closed.
  WHY: Two consecutive API failures leave the tracker closed with the racing entry on it, and the documented `reason=after_close_read_failed` log (:798) is never emitted.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:403 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The re-listing in `_reopen_tracker_after_post` uses per_page=30 with no pagination.
  WHY: With more than 30 open ai:operator-step trackers, the tracker can drop out of the listing, which triggers needless reopen PATCHes and wastes API budget.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:806-813 (check-run tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, run 43089754069, head 73372b31) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The only red check on the head cannot be mapped to any hunk of this PR: the collected tail (collection_status: timeout) ends inside `python3 tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py`, whose `[lint_pr_body_auto_close] ... #2734` error lines are that test's own fixture output (tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:275, :489).
  WHY: The check blocks the merge, and the real failing step lies outside the tail, so the editor must read the full job log (and the merge-base run) before acting; the PR body (`Closes .../issues/9203`, `Refs #8291`) complies with §21.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

(No task gaps reported.)

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:lines 638-648, _is_release_entry | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A step with no `dormant_until` counts as release-only when its title matches RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE (promote/tag/release/publish/cut/sync/propagate/roll out ... "stable"), and `dormant_until` is optional in the scripts/activation_verify.sh line 747 schema, so "Sync the DEPLOY_TOKEN secret to the stable environment" is safe only when the model also fills in `dormant_until`.
  WHY: Once `stable` contains the commit, resolve ticks the real human step and may close the tracker as completed, so the secret is never set; fix: add a negative check for secret/token/variable/setting/permission/account/key, or accept only titles that name the release mechanism.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (job tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, run 43089754069, head 73372b31) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The failed check cannot be mapped to any PR hunk (collection_status: timeout), and the visible `##[error][lint_pr_body_auto_close]` lines are fixtures at tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:275 and :489; the PR body (`Closes .../issues/9203`, `Refs #8291`) complies with §21.
  WHY: The check stays red and blocks merge, so the editor must read the full job log.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:resolve(), lines 792-799, with guard at line 762 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Any transient post-close comment-read failure (ApiError from load_entry_comments lines 367-376) reopens the tracker with `state_reason == "reopened"`, which line 762 cannot tell apart from a person's reopen.
  WHY: The tracker logs `outcome=open reason=reopened` forever and is never auto-closed again, which defeats "The issue closes when no unticked boxes remain"; fix: post an `ai:operator-step:auto-reopened reason=after_close_read_failed` marker and skip the guard when that marker is the newest trusted comment.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py, together with scripts/activation_verify.sh:`_reopen_tracker_after_post` raise; activation_verify.sh lines 753-758 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the entry POST succeeds and only the re-listing fails, upsert exits 2 and activation_verify.sh returns before the verdict comment (lines 762-804), with a WARNING that wrongly says the issue "could not be updated".
  WHY: The verdict marker is lost with no retry (PR mode none; project mode needs a trusted partial marker, and none is written); fix: use a distinct exit code (e.g. 3), warn accurately and continue to the verdict.
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: NONE (all P10 deliverables present; the pass-1 #2734 auto-close TASK_GAP was rejected as fixture strings).
- HARDENING: scripts/operator_step_issue.py resolve() line 797: wrap the reopen PATCH in try/except ApiError, log `reason=after_close_reopen_failed` and re-raise (5 lines); _reopen_tracker_after_post: log `outcome=error reason=listing_failed` instead of `outcome=skip` (2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:646 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The code falls back to title-based regex matching for release steps when dormant_until is empty.
  WHY: A human step (e.g. a secret sync) whose title matches the release regex is wrongly resolved and auto-ticked, so manual work may be skipped.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:782 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: There is a race between the initial state check (line 762) and the close PATCH (line 782).
  WHY: The tracker can be closed even though a person deliberately reopened it during the race window.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:797 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The reopen PATCH does not set state_reason=reopened.
  WHY: Future automated re-closes could fire despite an earlier deliberate reopen.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:345 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Prepending Note: to lines matching DORMANT_LINE_RE stops _unticked_steps from recognising them as dormant lines.
  WHY: Release steps are misread as human steps, so the tracker either closes too early or fails to resolve.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:403 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The re-listing in _reopen_tracker_after_post uses per_page=30 with no pagination.
  WHY: With more than 30 open trackers, the tracker can drop out of the listing, which causes needless reopen PATCHes.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:408-416 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Re-listing failures are logged with a generic reason and then raise ApiError, which hides the root cause in the caller's warning.
  WHY: Callers wrongly report the comment write as failed, although the comment was posted.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:752-754 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Failures during the after-close read log an error and raise ApiError, so the process exits 2.
  WHY: Callers wrongly report the write as failed, which misleads operators.
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: NONE
- HARDENING: line 398 (_reopen_tracker_after_post): print the error including the exception type before raising (1 line, risk 1); lines 794-799 (resolve): wrap the reopen PATCH in try/except and log after_close_reopen_failed before re-raising (4 lines, risk 2).
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
